note.backdrop: At midday the fall is wider and deeper than before the open: the S&P 500 fund -1.3% (it was -0.7%), the Nasdaq 100 fund -1.9% (-1.3%), small caps -1.2% (-0.5%), the VIX +8.9%. No market-wide flag and no fear flag. The median of the 2,450 stocks is -0.8% and 71% of them are lower. AI stocks led a broader sell-off (Dow Jones): Asian technology indexes closed sharply lower, and a strategist at XTB ties today's selling to fears that Congress will tighten limits on chips that may reach China, cutting spending on chips and data centers. Nvidia reports on Tuesday after the close; Anthropic's shares are expected to price at $70 to $78, a valuation near $1.4 trillion (Invezz). Rates are not the cause today: Treasuries strengthened and the 10-year yield is down 0.02 point, near 5.13% (Dow Jones). Oil is -2.6%, gold -0.4%, the dollar +0.1%. Bitcoin is -4.9% from Friday's close, about $64,900, little changed since the morning. Money is moving as well as leaving: health insurers, food makers and some software are up. Six stocks are outside their 9-in-10 range and 48 outside their 2-in-3 range.

read.says: Dow Jones: AI stocks led a broader sell-off before Nvidia's results on Tuesday and the pricing of Anthropic's offering; Asian technology indexes closed sharply lower; XTB's strategist ties the selling to fears that Republicans and Democrats will combine to tighten limits on chips that may go to China, cutting spending on chips and data centers; the 10-year yield fell to about 5.13%; Brent fell 1% to below $95.

The Nasdaq opened 1.5% lower and the S&P 500 about 1%; Nvidia lost 13% last week; the weakness reached AI infrastructure (CoreWeave -5.2%, Nebius -8%, IREN, Applied Digital, Core Scientific); Anthropic is reported to target a valuation of about $1.4 trillion with shares priced between $70 and $78; a Financial Times report says Nvidia's former chief is considering a return.

After Friday's close the federal Medicaid agency offered states an optional transition period to June 30, 2027 for the new Medicaid work rules, during which states will not deny or drop otherwise eligible people solely for failing them; Centene rose 2.5% and Molina 2.6% in extended trading.
Molina rose just over 8% on Monday morning to $226.47 as managed-care peers also gained: Centene just over 5%, Elevance almost 4%; the report gives no cause.
On Nov 4 Molina rose 7.5% to $223.36 and Centene 8.9% after brokerages said the election result lowered policy risk for Medicaid-focused insurers and hospitals.

Trump Media fell 12% to $4.10 ahead of a $976.8 million convertible-note obligation with a near-term demand feature and a shareholder vote on its TAE merger; it is down 43% in a month; Rumble fell almost as hard as speculative and AI-linked stocks sold off, with funding needs and softer guidance weighing on it.

Financial Times: Trump Media faces a Nov 30 deadline to repay up to $1 billion of convertible bonds that convert at $34.72 against a share price of $4.64; it may have to sell assets including crypto holdings worth about $1.36 billion at the end of the third quarter, or borrow at high cost; it lost $234 million in nine months.

After the FDA's letter Barclays cut its Summit target to $18 from $20 (Equal Weight) and Citi to $42 from $43 (Buy), Jefferies kept Buy at $30; Barclays sees limited direct effect on value but what seems a higher FDA bar for the lung cancer program.

Espey's first fiscal quarter: sales $10.6 million against $9.1 million, net income $2.19 million against $2.17 million, new orders $2.6 million against $10.5 million a year earlier, backlog $126.7 million against $141.1 million.
Clearwater Paper named a new finance chief and said repairs at its Augusta mill after disruptions in late September and October are largely complete, with the mill returning to normal operations.
Oxford Square Capital reported net asset value of $1.21 a share at Sept 30 (from $1.29) and declared monthly distributions of $0.015 a share for January to March 2027.

Icahn Enterprises: a $0.50 distribution to holders of record on Nov 16, 2026; indicative net asset value about $3.5 billion at Sept 30; its stake in CVR Energy valued at $4.2 billion; $522 million of losses on refining hedges in its funds in the third quarter.
Genco's $1.05 per share dividend goes to holders of record on Nov 16, 2026.

singles.beneath: Part of it has a visible source. Its largest holding, CVR Energy, is down 5.6% today as oil falls 2.6%. The Nov 3 release valued that stake at $4.2 billion, while the whole of Icahn Enterprises was worth about $3.6 billion at Friday's close (its net asset value was about $3.5 billion at Sept 30). So CVR's fall alone is worth roughly 6 to 7 points of the 14 by arithmetic; that is my inference. Its funds also hold hedges against refiners, which lost $522 million last quarter when refiners rose and should gain when they fall; I cannot size that. About half the net fall has no source I can find. This morning I called the flag an artifact of the distribution: that was right for the 10.5%, and is no longer the whole story.
singles.cause: Icahn Enterprises is -23.6% on the check, at about $3.59 against Friday's $4.74. Of that, $0.50 is the distribution that left the price today (10.5%). Net of it the units are down about 14%, on 3.26 million units by midday, as many as all of Friday. No filing and no story explains it.

themes.beneath: One element is new since the morning and is reported: the worry about a law limiting chip sales, on top of Nvidia's first report under an interim chief on Tuesday evening and Anthropic's offering, expected to price at $70 to $78 a share for a valuation near $1.4 trillion. None of these is a fact about orders: no page I read reports a customer cutting spending. Where the money went shows in what rose: software (Adobe +2.9%, Intuit +2.5%, Workday +1.5%), health insurers and food makers.
themes.cause: By midday the fall reaches every layer of AI spending. Sellers of computing capacity: IREN -9.8%, Applied Digital -8.5%, CoreWeave -6.2%. Networking and optics: Lumentum -7.8%, Coherent -6.0%, Ciena -5.9%, Arista -5.3%. Memory and storage: Sandisk -7.3%, Micron -6.3%, Seagate -5.6%. Power and cooling: Bloom -6.8%, Vertiv -6.5%. Chip equipment: Teradyne -6.3%, Lam -5.5%. Chips: Intel -7.0%, Marvell -6.3%, AMD -4.8%, Broadcom -3.7%, Nvidia -3.5%; the median of 59 chip stocks is -4.9% (it was -4.0% before the open). Buyers: Oracle -4.7%, Alphabet -3.0%, Amazon -2.9%, Meta -2.2%, while Microsoft is -0.2% and Apple -0.8%. Dow Jones reports AI stocks leading a broader sell-off and quotes XTB's strategist: the fear is that Congress tightens limits on chips that may reach China, which would cut spending on chips and data centers. Invezz reports the weakness reaching AI infrastructure companies.
themes.mechanism: The morning's question is answered: the fall did spread to the buyers, all but Microsoft and Apple. The size of each fall follows how much a company depends on AI spending continuing: capacity sellers and optics most, then memory, power and equipment, then the chip makers, then the buyers. Nvidia itself is falling less than almost everything that sells into the build-out. My inference: the market is marking down the spending, not one company. Power Solutions (-11.9%, no news) has CoreWeave and IREN among the stocks it moved with over the year and a beta near 3, so I read it as part of this group; that too is inference.
themes.name: The AI sell-off spread from chips to the whole build-out and to most of the buyers

read_through.why: The metal mining group is down 5.8% at the median (Southern Copper -4.5%, MP Materials -5.8%, USA Rare Earth -10.7%). Copper and rare earths go into data centers and power equipment, so the same markdown may be reaching them, but I read no page today that says so.

themes.watch: Nvidia's results and outlook on Tuesday evening. Whether a bill on chip limits exists or it is only talk. The price Anthropic's shares are set at. Whether Microsoft and Apple keep holding.

themes.beneath: Two stories now overlap in these stocks: bitcoin's fall, tied by reports to rate expectations, and the sell-off in speculative shares that the AI markdown set off. Chaince Digital (CD) fell another 19.2% with no filing and no story; after Friday's -18.7% that is about -34% in two sessions, and still unexplained.
themes.cause: Bitcoin is -4.9% from Friday's close, about $64,900, and has stayed between about $64,100 and $65,300 through the session. The large holders are near their usual rates: Strategy -7.6% (its rate implies -6.4%), Coinbase -6.0% (-5.2%), SBET -4.6% (-6.1%), BMNR -5.3% (-6.7%). Two small ones have fallen well past theirs: Forward Industries -11.2% (-5.9% implied) and ASST -10.5% (-7.4%). Trump Media is -12.2% and Rumble -13.3%. The Financial Times reported on Saturday that Trump Media must repay up to $1 billion of convertible bonds by Nov 30 and may have to sell assets, including some of its crypto; 24/7 Wall St puts the obligation at $976.8 million and adds a shareholder vote on its merger with TAE. The same report says Rumble is falling with speculative stocks, with funding needs and softer guidance weighing on it.
themes.mechanism: The bonds convert into stock at $34.72 and the stock is near $4.10, so holders have every reason to ask for cash instead (FT). Trump Media's most valuable asset is crypto worth about $1.36 billion at the end of September. Its own rate to bitcoin is low (0.39 per 1%), so bitcoin carried only -1.9% of today's -12.2%: this is mostly its own trouble. A company that may have to sell bitcoin within two weeks is also a reason for other holders of bitcoin to be marked down; that step is my inference, and it may be part of why the small treasuries fell past their rates.
themes.name: Crypto: bitcoin steady since the morning; Trump Media's debt deadline adds a second pressure
themes.watch: Any filing by Trump Media about the notes before Nov 30, and whether it sells bitcoin. Bitcoin against its weekend low of $62,040. Whether the small treasuries keep falling past their usual rates.

themes.beneath: This answers the morning's unexplained Molina move: the pre-market rise was real and has doubled, on 1.7 million shares by midday against 0.36 million all Friday. In proportion, Molina at about $228 is now above the $223.36 it reached in the rally after the Nov 4 election.
themes.cause: After Friday's close the federal Medicaid agency offered states an optional transition period to June 30, 2027 for the new work rules: during it, states will not deny or drop otherwise eligible people solely for failing them (Rallies, Nov 13). Centene and Molina rose 2.5% and 2.6% in extended trading that evening. Today Molina is +9.1%, outside its 9-in-10 range, Centene +4.9%, Elevance +3.6%, Humana +2.1%, Cigna +1.0%, UnitedHealth +0.9%.
themes.mechanism: Fewer people losing Medicaid in the first half of 2027 means more members for the insurers that run Medicaid plans, and the two that reports call Medicaid-focused, Molina and Centene, are up the most. No page dated today states the cause of Monday's rise (TokenPost reports the move without one), so tying it to Friday's decision is my inference. It also fits the day's move out of AI and into defensive groups.
themes.name: Medicaid insurers rise after enforcement of the work rules was eased
themes.watch: An analyst note or company statement that names the cause. Whether states take up the transition period. The insurers' guidance for 2027 membership.

themes.beneath: Nov 22 is a Sunday, so Capricor's answer comes within the week. Summit's fall has not deepened much since the open (-13.1% before it, -14.9% now).
themes.cause: Summit is -14.9% in the session after Sunday's FDA letter. Barclays cut its target to $18 from $20 and Citi to $42 from $43, and Jefferies kept $30; Barclays sees little direct effect on value but what seems a higher FDA bar for the lung cancer program (Stocktwits, citing The Fly). Capricor is -12.5% with no filing of its own; headlines in its feed say its holders are nervous after Summit's rejection, with its own FDA decision due by Nov 22.
themes.mechanism: Summit was refused because a trial that slowed the disease did not show a significant survival benefit. Investors in other companies waiting on the FDA read that as a stricter agency; the headlines report that reading for Capricor.
themes.name: After Summit's rejection, nerves about the next FDA decisions

read_through.why: A headline says Savara has an FDA deadline on the same date; it is -2.5% today. Whether a rejection at one company moves others waiting on the FDA has not been tested here.

themes.watch: Capricor's decision by Nov 22; what Summit says about its next step with the FDA.

themes.beneath: The wider lesson is about pre-market prints. Of this morning's seven moves that rested on a few pre-market trades, only Molina's held and grew. Dianthus went from -6.7% to -2.6%, Immunocore from +6.9% to -1.8%, Ideaya from +6.6% to -1.3%, Aramark from -5.5% to +0.9%, UroGen from -10.2% to +8.4%; Corsair kept part (-6.5% to -4.1%).
themes.cause: CG Oncology opened at $89.30 (+20%), fell to $78.78 within fifteen minutes and was +12.2% on the check's reading (about $87 a little later), on 7.85 million shares against 3.31 million all Friday. UroGen opened 9.1% lower at $23.81, then rose to about $28 (+8.4% on the check's reading), on 1.79 million shares against 0.70 million all Friday.
themes.mechanism: This morning I inferred that UroGen fell before the open because CG Oncology's result threatens it. That did not hold: the stock is up on the day. Either buyers read the result as proof that this disease is a large market for more than one drug, or the pre-market fall was thin trading that the session corrected. I found no page that explains UroGen's move in either direction, and the article on CG Oncology I tried to read was refused.
themes.name: Bladder cancer: CG Oncology kept part of its jump; UroGen reversed and my morning inference did not hold
themes.watch: Any analyst note on what the result means for UroGen. CG Oncology's full data on Dec 2.
